meta.title: tenant-pi installed environment
meta.intro: A runtime map, not a host scan. Core is required. Optional means selectable; configured means supplied with settings and credentials; verified means a recorded check of the stated behavior. This page verifies no live service.

placeholders.pi_bin: the pi command of your npm prefix
placeholders.aliases: the model aliases of the gateway
placeholders.mcp_servers: the MCP servers that you define

views.label: Installed environment
views.summary: Start at your terminal. One Pi process uses the selected profile, local files and your chosen model route. Optional modules add memory and service calls; these are capabilities, not an inventory of your machine.

groups.label: Local files and code
groups.sub: Profile, account and project have different lifetimes

groups.label: Service endpoints
groups.sub: Only the routes and modules you use

nodes.label: User terminal
nodes.summary: You interact with Pi in a terminal. The launcher selects {{profile}} through PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR. It runs {{pi_bin}} from your shell PATH.

nodes.label: Herdr workspace
nodes.summary: Herdr can host the terminal and other agent panes. Its skill and application are separate choices. The application is {{herdr_bin}}. A plain terminal needs neither. Herdr-hosted Pi is not qualified.

nodes.label: Pi runtime
nodes.summary: Pi runs as your operating-system account, using {{profile}}/settings.json. A profile selects configuration and state; it is not an OS sandbox. Local tools keep the account permissions.

nodes.label: Enabled modules
nodes.summary: Pi loads only the selected resources declared by the profile and other trusted resource scopes. Core works without these optional modules. Skills provide instructions; extensions add runtime behavior. The catalog shows available modules, not enabled modules on this machine.

nodes.label: Profile state
nodes.summary: Pi writes login and sessions under {{profile}}. Enabled Hermes stores session indexes and memory there too. A new candidate gets none of this state. Authentication is not copied between profiles.

nodes.label: Account memory
nodes.summary: Optional LLM Wiki uses {{wiki_vault}} or a project vault. OpenViking client queues and logs live under ~/.openviking/. These paths are outside the selected profile and can be shared by profiles of the account. Recall text can enter model requests.

nodes.label: Working project
nodes.summary: Core tools read and edit files and run shell commands with account permissions. A trusted project can add resource and settings overrides.

nodes.label: Runtime module sources
nodes.summary: Optional in-tree code stays at {{clone}}/packages/. Generated profiles refer to its absolute paths; keep the clone in place. The AgentCore extension imports the shared memory core in packages/agentcore-memory-core. The Claude Code plugin packages/agentcore-claude and the owner tool packages/agentcore-memory-admin use the same core; no profile loads them. Other selected modules load from the profile npm directory. The clone is a code source, not a running service.

nodes.label: Chosen model route
nodes.summary: Pi sends prompt context and tool results through the selected route. Native provider login and direct inference do not require a gateway. The optional gateway forwards requests to an upstream provider.

nodes.label: Remote memory
nodes.summary: Only enabled and configured clients contact these services. OpenViking recalls memories and can capture turns. AgentCore sends each typed prompt to AWS as a recall query and has no capture path. Its propose tool sends a text only after the person confirms it. Both need the two memory consents.

nodes.label: Tool and service calls
nodes.summary: Optional tools send their call inputs to configured services and return results to Pi. Some enabled modules also make startup or automatic calls. Endpoint configuration proves neither access nor a successful call.

boundaries.label: Your account / runtime host
boundaries.sub: Local process and files; account permissions still apply

boundaries.label: Outside the Pi process
boundaries.sub: Same host, LAN or remote; not installed by this page

views.label: Profile & files
views.summary: A selected profile is a directory, not a separate account. The launcher chooses it; Pi and enabled modules use several storage scopes. No authentication state moves to a new profile.

groups.label: Configuration and state
groups.sub: Paths are examples, not detected values

nodes.label: Launcher
nodes.summary: The launcher in {{private}} starts {{pi_bin}} with {{profile}} as the agent directory. It removes inherited PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR. It inherits other environment values, including provider keys.

nodes.label: Pi session
nodes.summary: Pi creates auth.json after login and sessions during use. The kit copies no authentication or session state from another profile.

nodes.label: Selected resources
nodes.summary: Directory package filters select enabled extensions and skills. OpenViking and AgentCore instead load their index.ts as local-file sources. Additional owner packages and trusted project resources are possible.

nodes.label: Core file and shell tools
nodes.summary: The profile does not confine tool access to its own directory. Trusted project settings can override profile choices. Project trust is a separate launch-time decision.

nodes.label: Optional memory clients
nodes.summary: Hermes is profile-scoped. LLM Wiki can be account- or project-scoped. OpenViking client state is account-shared. Server memories are separate from these local paths.

nodes.label: Selected profile settings
nodes.summary: Settings hold package sources, filters and defaults. Optional mcp-adapter.json and hermes-memory-config.json live beside them. models.json registers direct inference, from the owner or from a validated inputs.modelsFile. .tenant-pi/ holds generation records, not a runtime daemon.

nodes.label: Profile-owned runtime state
nodes.summary: These files belong to this profile. A new candidate starts without its login, sessions, installed npm modules or Hermes store. MCP can spill output to the temporary directory outside the profile.

nodes.label: Code stays at its source
nodes.summary: In-tree runtime modules are loaded by absolute path from this clone. npm modules reside under the profile npm directory. Moving the clone breaks those path references. A kit update can change code loaded by an existing profile.

nodes.label: Project files and settings
nodes.summary: Pi tools can read and write the project. Trusted .pi/settings.json can add settings and resources.

nodes.label: Shared account state
nodes.summary: The wiki vault {{wiki_vault}}, ~/.openviking/ and the operating-system keyring are outside the selected profile. Other profiles of this account can share them. The fallback {{live}} stays separate; a new candidate does not import it.

views.label: Models & services
views.summary: Choose one model route per request; the first three rows are alternatives. The other rows are optional service clients, not mandatory steps in inference. Every endpoint needs separate configuration and verification.

groups.label: Outside the Pi process
groups.sub: Same host or remote; data recipient

nodes.label: A. Native provider
nodes.summary: Pi can use its native provider directly, without codex-accounts or a gateway. Login state belongs to the selected profile; a shell API key is another credential source.

nodes.label: B. Direct inference
nodes.summary: Pi reads custom provider registrations from {{profile}}/models.json. generate writes it only from a validated inputs.modelsFile; the owner can also write it. llama-swap and vLLM are examples. Neither needs the optional Tenantext gateway. Registration does not prove reachability.

nodes.label: C. Gateway client
nodes.summary: This optional route reads TENANTEXT_LITELLM_BASE_URL and TENANTEXT_LITELLM_API_KEY from its process environment. The gateway key is not the native provider login. The supported route uses an HTTPS endpoint ending in /v1.

nodes.label: MCP adapter
nodes.summary: MCP means Model Context Protocol. The adapter exposes tools from configured servers. Exclusive mode uses the profile definitions and disables built-in MCP. Lazy servers connect on use; eager servers can connect at startup. OAuth can use the shared OS keyring.

nodes.label: Knowledge and workflow skills
nodes.summary: Selected knowledge and workflow tools can use OpenKnowledge and a Gitea tracker. A skill file does not install its tools or services. Requests carry the task or page content needed for that operation.

nodes.label: Usage and decision clients
nodes.summary: Enabled usage modules and doctor can send account tokens to provider usage endpoints. A configured context-meter nextMoveUrl can receive session counters and the last 300 characters of the user message. Its default URL is empty.

nodes.label: Native model provider
nodes.summary: The selected native provider receives prompt context, including tool results and recalled memory included by the session. No gateway is required. Credentials and model availability need a live check.

nodes.label: Direct inference server
nodes.summary: A local or LAN inference endpoint receives model requests directly from Pi. Its authentication and transport follow the owner registration. A local endpoint can still forward data elsewhere.

nodes.label: Gateway and its upstream
nodes.summary: On route C only, {{gateway}} receives the request and forwards it to {{provider}}. It resolves {{aliases}}. Both gateway and upstream receive model data. The kit installs neither service.

nodes.label: Configured MCP servers
nodes.summary: The adapter passes tool arguments to the selected server and returns its results to Pi. A server can run as a local stdio process or a remote HTTP service. Disabled definitions never connect.

nodes.label: Knowledge / tracker services
nodes.summary: Knowledge calls use {{ok_service}} through its tools. Tracker calls use the configured repository service. These services receive selected pages, task text or issue content; none is implied by a core install.

nodes.label: Usage / decision endpoints
nodes.summary: Provider usage endpoints can receive an existing account credential. A separately configured decision server receives the counters and prompt suffix described by context-meter. These are not model-route dependencies.

views.label: Memory & data
views.summary: All four memory modules are optional. Local storage does not mean local-only model context: recalled text can enter the chosen model request. Configuration and consent permit behavior; they do not prove that a live operation succeeds.

nodes.label: Hermes
nodes.summary: Enabling Hermes indexes sessions and provides memory tools. Automatic review defaults off in the recommended choices. Enabling review needs roles.memory; explicit model-backed commands can still call a model.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki
nodes.summary: Wiki tools read and write pages. With ambientPersonalVault on, vault text can enter each prompt. A trusted project vault or settings override changes scope. Ingest can use the session model or a configured task model.

nodes.label: OpenViking client
nodes.summary: The enabled client asks for memories before user prompts and can send session turns to its server. Tool-result output is included only with captureToolResults true. Credentials and identity come from external configuration, not this kit.

nodes.label: AgentCore client
nodes.summary: AgentCore recall sends each typed prompt to AWS as the search query. The tool agentcore_propose writes one proposal only after the person confirms the text and the target namespace. The extension has no capture path. Both memory consents are required. It uses the AWS profile of the person config, else the AWS SDK credential chain. It imports the shared core packages/agentcore-memory-core; the Claude Code plugin packages/agentcore-claude uses the same core. The owner's reviewed submit to /shared/ and /actor/ is a separate approval-gated path.

nodes.label: Wiki embeddings
nodes.summary: An embedding is a numeric representation used for similarity search. Embeddings are off unless explicitly configured with embeddingTextTransfer consent. Backfill is a separate operation, not a consequence of installing the kit.

nodes.label: Context and background work
nodes.sub: Model data can leave local storage
nodes.summary: Recall added to a prompt reaches the selected model route. Hermes review and wiki synthesis can make additional model calls. Turning automatic review off does not prevent a model call from an explicitly invoked tool.

nodes.label: Profile-local memory
nodes.summary: Hermes writes memory files, project memories and pi-hermes-memory/sessions.db under {{profile}}. A new profile starts with a different store; no migration is implied.

nodes.label: Account or project wiki
nodes.summary: A project .llm-wiki vault can win over the personal vault. Personal state normally lives outside the profile. Profiles of the same account can use the same vault, so switching profiles does not roll its data back.

nodes.label: OpenViking server
nodes.summary: The server stores sessions and memories and returns recall. Client pending queues, ledgers and logs stay under ~/.openviking/, shared by the account. Server-side processing and its downstream services depend on the server configuration.

nodes.label: AWS AgentCore Memory
nodes.summary: AWS stores the records and returns matches from the namespaces of the person's policy. A recall sends the prompt as the query. A propose call writes one confirmed text to the proposals namespace of the person; a maintainer of the project reviews it. No capture path exists. The owner tool packages/agentcore-memory-admin renders the IAM policy of each person. Live AWS behavior remains unverified.

nodes.label: Chosen embedding endpoint
nodes.summary: The selected endpoint receives page text at write time and search queries during vector recall. Vectors stay in meta/embeddings.json. Endpoint compatibility and retrieval quality need separate verification.

nodes.label: Chosen model route
nodes.summary: A native provider, direct inference server or optional gateway receives the model context. Local memory storage does not keep that context on this host. Background tasks can use roles.memory when configured.

views.label: Module catalog
views.summary: Available modules, not a detected installation. Core is required; every other module is optional. Manifest status and source checks are not proof of a working client. Select a card for inputs, consent, dependencies and readiness gaps.

nodes.label: core
nodes.summary: Pi itself at the pin. The only component that is always on. Each other component requires it.

nodes.label: model-routing
nodes.summary: Builtin Pi settings for the default provider, model and thinking level, and the model cycle.
nodes.inputs: roles, optional modelRoutes; --registry when modelRoutes names a model

nodes.label: tenantext
nodes.summary: The base Tenantext extension of the in-tree package.

nodes.label: codex-accounts
nodes.summary: Optional gateway routing client. Native provider login and direct inference work without this module. The supported kit gateway configuration uses an environment key, not the native login.

nodes.label: context-meter
nodes.summary: Shows the context use of the session. ops-footer needs it.

nodes.label: ops-footer
nodes.summary: A footer with usage readings and health checks. It receives the readings of the usage components.

nodes.label: copilot-usage
nodes.summary: Reads the Copilot quota. It reads login files and environment tokens of the account and sends one to the usage endpoint.

nodes.label: anthropic-usage
nodes.summary: Reads the Claude quota with an active login, read-only. Mode off sends nothing.

nodes.label: doctor
nodes.summary: Checks the setup of the Tenantext extensions and reports on the extensions that are not enabled.

nodes.label: resources
nodes.summary: Manages the resource selections of the profile: toggles in settings.json.

nodes.label: hermes
nodes.summary: Local memory in the profile: hermes-memory-config.json and runtime memory files. It uses the native module better-sqlite3.
nodes.inputs: memory.hermes; roles.memory when backgroundReview is true

nodes.label: wiki
nodes.summary: LLM Wiki: profile settings and a personal vault outside the target. An existing vault is used as it is.

nodes.label: openviking
nodes.summary: The vendored OpenViking extension. It writes sessions and memories to a separately configured OpenViking server.
nodes.inputs: memory.openviking; npm ci --ignore-scripts in packages/openviking-pi; a server

nodes.label: agentcore
nodes.summary: Optional shared AgentCore Memory on the memory core: recall before each typed prompt and the confirmed propose tool agentcore_propose. OpenViking stays primary. The extension has no capture path.
nodes.inputs: memory.agentcore.configFile; npm ci --ignore-scripts in packages/agentcore-memory-core; an AWS resource

nodes.label: coordinator-skills
nodes.summary: Skills for a coordinator: grilling, wayfinder, research, prototype, specs and tickets, review, status. They name host tools that the kit does not install.
nodes.inputs: a Gitea tracker for to-spec, to-tickets and wayfinder

nodes.label: knowledge-skills
nodes.summary: Skills for OpenKnowledge and the Open Knowledge Format. The MCP server and the ok command are external tools.
nodes.inputs: the OpenKnowledge MCP server and the ok command

nodes.label: tracker-site
nodes.summary: A skill that builds a tracker brief and site from the repository and its issue tracker.
nodes.inputs: Python 3.11 and Git on PATH; PYTHONPATH set to packages/tenantext

nodes.label: herdr
nodes.summary: The Herdr skill. Agent fan-out goes through it. It does not install the Herdr application.

nodes.label: herdr-relay
nodes.summary: Runs a shell command through a standing worker pane. Optional and off by default.
nodes.inputs: herdr enabled, the herdr tool, Python 3

nodes.label: herdr-watch
nodes.summary: A Pi extension that starts a task session in a Herdr pane or prompts a pane that exists, waits on it in the background, and delivers the reply as a task notification.
nodes.inputs: herdr enabled, the herdr tool, Python 3, the herdr skill scripts

nodes.label: questions
nodes.summary: The Pi question extension at an exact version. It gives Pi the ask_user_question tool.

nodes.label: mcp
nodes.summary: The MCP adapter with definitions from a private input file. It disables the native Pi MCP and runs in exclusive mode.

tour.title: Start with the terminal
tour.text: Use a plain terminal or an optional Herdr workspace. Your launcher chooses the Pi profile for that process.

tour.title: One process, one selected profile
tour.text: The profile selects settings and state. It is not an operating-system sandbox; tools retain the account permissions.

tour.title: Only selected modules
tour.text: Core Pi needs no optional module. Extensions add behavior; skills add instructions. The catalog is not a report of what this host installed.

tour.title: Model routes are alternatives
tour.text: Native provider login, direct inference and the optional gateway are three routes. A request does not have to pass through all three.

tour.title: Authentication stays in its profile
tour.text: A new candidate does not get the old auth.json or sessions. Log in again. The launcher can still inherit shell credentials.

tour.title: Some state is shared
tour.text: The personal wiki and OpenViking client state live outside the profile. Switching profiles is not a rollback of that shared data.

tour.title: Know each data recipient
tour.text: Remote recall sends prompts to the chosen memory service. AgentCore has no capture path; its propose tool writes only a confirmed text. Recalled text can then reach the model provider.

tour.title: Configuration is not verification
tour.text: Manifest status, selected resources and reachable endpoints are different evidence. Record live checks separately; this offline page does not run them.
